title: Rocket Report: FAA eyes more Starbase traffic; India's Skyroot snares US customer
gist: Ars Technica's Rocket Report 9.15 covers Rocket Lab's Neutron slipping to 2027, SpaceX seeking FAA approval for 456 Starship launches a year at Starbase, Reflect Orbital buying launches from India's Skyroot, and new entrants LEAP and Stoke Space.

insights.claim: Reflect Orbital bought two launches from India's Skyroot Aerospace (Vikram-1 and Vikram-1U), and the article says this reflects satellite operators' fear of a coming under-supply of US launch capacity as SpaceX phases out Falcon 9 for the relatively unproven Starship.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Launch scarcity could favor alternative providers; watch Falcon 9 retirement timing.

insights.claim: Reflect Orbital plans a constellation of some 50,000 mirrors to beam sunlight to the ground for power and illumination, with its first satellite launching on a Falcon 9 rideshare next year after FCC approval earlier this year.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: An exploratory business model with regulatory sign-off on the first satellite.

insights.claim: LEAP, a Colorado startup, aims to enter dedicated small-satellite launch in 2028 with the Bighorn rocket (145 kg to LEO) and a Denver-area factory producing six vehicles a year, scalable to two per month.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Small-launch competition is expanding in response to demand.
insights.quote: “We know how to build remarkable vehicles. The challenge is building enough of them fast enough,”

insights.claim: Rocket Lab said Neutron will not fly until 2027 because of voids in the carbon-composite forward dome of the first-stage propellant tank, publicly confirming what the industry already knew.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Another Neutron delay hurts Rocket Lab's medium-lift timeline versus competitors.

insights.claim: Carbon composites are lighter, stronger and corrosion resistant but generally harder to manufacture than metal, and the article reads the latest issue as Rocket Lab still struggling with the large booster stage.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Manufacturing yield, not design, is the risk to watch for Neutron.

insights.claim: Stoke Space shipped Nova's reusable second stage to Moses Lake for cryo-proof and Andromeda hotfire testing, aiming to launch Nova next year; the article calls it the only fully reusable Western rocket besides Starship in advanced development.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Stoke is the nearest fully reusable Starship competitor to track.
insights.locator: Stoke ships second stage for testing

insights.claim: SpaceX has asked the FAA to allow up to 456 launches and 912 landings a year at Starbase, about 18 times the currently allowed 25 launches and 50 landings.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Regulatory approval would be a gating item for Starship cadence.
insights.locator: Let us launch more, SpaceX asks FAA

insights.claim: Elon Musk says the first Starship landing back at Starbase could come as soon as the next test flight later this year, and SpaceX has already landed boosters there.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A Starship catch would be a key milestone for reusability claims.

insights.claim: Ship 40, the first Starship to survive an ocean splashdown, returned to Starbase for inspection that SpaceX says will give first-of-its-kind data on a flown heatshield, Raptor engines and avionics.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Reuse data feeds the path to rapid reusability.
insights.quote: “provide first-of-its-kind data on a flown Starship heatshield, Raptor engines, avionics, and more,”

insights.claim: A SpaceX Falcon 9 launched the Space Development Agency's fourth Tranche 1 Transport Layer plane, the first batch from Northrop Grumman, after an October 5 abort and two further delays.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Shows SDA's constellation progressing and the contractor mix.
insights.locator: Falcon 9 launches US military data transport satellites

insights.claim: SpaceX completed its 35th ISS resupply mission, delivering 6,322 pounds including two roll-out solar arrays and payloads for more than 40 experiments.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Routine cadence of NASA cargo service.
